To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GH and/or IGF-I treatment in the elderly is associated with a number of beneficial effects including increased lean body mass, increased strength, increased bone mineral density, and decreased fat mass.

GH and/or IGF-I replacement in healthy elderly subjects is associated with beneficial effects on muscle mass, strength, and physical function, but that there is no evidence of a significant impact on mortality or morbidity.

the GH/IGF axis is a key regulator of the aging process, and the administration of GH and/or IGF-I to elderly subjects can improve body composition, physical performance, and quality of the aging process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of the somatotropic decline in aging and how this decline may be corrected.
the effects of aging on the GHRH-GH axis and the effects of GH and/or IGF-I on the function of muscle and bone.
determining the mechanisms by which the somatopause leads to the loss of muscle and bone mass, the loss of strength and functional capacity, and the loss of quality of life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment of the somatopausal state with GH and IGF-1 has not been shown to be safe or effective.
GH replacement therapy for elderly subjects with the somatopause should be undertaken only after a careful assessment of potential risks and benefits.
GH/IGF therapy for the somotopause has not been proven to be beneficial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GH/IGF axis has a major role in the maintenance of lean body mass in elderly subjects.
GH and IGF therapy in the elderly can be beneficial, but the risks and benefits of such therapy need to be carefully weighed.
GH and IGF-1 therapy can be effective, but the risk/benefit ratio is not favorable for all subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GH-IGF axis is not a single entity.
GH and IGF-1 are not the only hormones that decline with age and that the decline in other hormones may be the primary cause for the functional decline in aging.
GH/IGF-1 replacement therapy is not without risk and that the benefits of such treatment are marginal at best.
